name: BHFS pattern (rodent LI-rTMS timing) at Oz
origin: Rodger lab (UWA, Perth) and Sherrard lab (Sorbonne); pattern from Global Energy Medicine patent PCT/AU2007/000454
summary: Copies the timing of 'biomimetic high-frequency stimulation' (BHFS, Grehl et al. 2016) from rodent low-intensity rTMS studies: 62.6-ms trains of 20 pulses repeated at 6.55 Hz for 1 min, 9.75 Hz for 8 min and 6.15 Hz for 1 min, on one coil at Oz. The rodent studies used 8 to 13 mT; this helmet gives 5 uT at 20 mm (8.4 uT at its maximum), 950 to 2,600 times less.
notes: Grehl et al. 2016 define BHFS as 300-us trapezoid pulses with a rise of 100 to 230 us, 108,840 per 10-min session (Grehl 2016 p.8; Dufor 2019 p.10). Effects are reported in mice, rats and cultures at 8 to 13 mT (Dufor 2019 p.10; Seewoo 2018 p.3). The same work found a floor: explants stimulated at 4.5 mT did not differ from sham, and the authors conclude that the field 'must be above a baseline intensity' (Dufor 2019 p.2). This program plays the three stages on one coil at Oz with no fade, so they keep their exact train counts (393, 4680 and 369). Each 300-us pulse becomes one 0.5-ms step at full scale, so the fast rise is lost. The sources give no spacing for the 20 pulses inside a train; the table spaces them evenly at 3.13 ms (62.6 ms / 20). Every pulse onset lands within about 0.5 ms of its exact time on the 2-kHz grid. No human placement exists: the coil at Oz is an arbitrary probe after the mouse visual-cortex work of Makowiecki et al. 2014, which used a related pattern (59.9-ms trains at 6.67, 10.01 and 6.25 Hz, about 8 mT). The rodent fields are 8 to 13 mT at the target tissue. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 5 uT (8.4 uT at the helmet's maximum) it is 950 to 2,600 times weaker, and the 4.5 mT that did nothing is still 530 times the helmet's maximum. All evidence is from rodents and cultures, from two labs that publish together; Dufor 2019 claim a mechanism that depends on cryptochrome. No human data exist at any strength, and this is not a treatment. Not for people with epilepsy; stop if you feel unwell.
setting: No human setting is published; all data are from rodents and cell cultures.
schedule: Rodent protocols ran 10 min a day for 14 days (Dufor 2019) or once a week for 4 weeks (Seewoo 2018). No human schedule has been tested.
source: Grehl et al. 2016, Front Neural Circuits (BHFS definition and device) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5093126/ ; Dufor et al. 2019, Sci Adv https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6821463/ ; Moretti & Rodger 2022 (LI-rTMS review) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9846462/ ; Seewoo et al. 2018, Sci Rep (coil and field) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5928106/ ; Makowiecki et al. 2014, J Neurosci (BHFS-like pattern over mouse visual cortex) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25100609/ ; Global Energy Medicine, patent PCT/AU2007/000454 (cited by Grehl 2016)
